answers.stem_only: Use Aurora point-in-time restore (within the 7-day retention) to 14:04; it always creates a new DB cluster, so restore to a new cluster and copy the deleted rows back (or repoint the app). Replicas share the cluster volume and already lost the rows; Sunday snapshot loses days of data; there is no in-place PITR.
Relational, join-heavy OLTP with PostgreSQL skills and a managed service: Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL (or RDS for PostgreSQL).

Encryption at rest cannot be turned on for an existing unencrypted Aurora cluster. Take a cluster snapshot, restore it to a new cluster encrypted with the customer managed KMS key (or copy the snapshot with encryption first), then cut the application over in the window.
Aurora Auto Scaling for Aurora Replicas with a target tracking policy on average reader CPU utilization; replicas are added at the peak and removed at night, and the reader endpoint picks them up.

I/O-Optimized pays off only when I/O is a large share of the spend (around a quarter or more), because instance and storage prices are higher. At 10 percent, stay on Aurora Standard; for a steady multi-year load, buy Reserved Instances for all three DB instances.
Aurora global database with a secondary cluster in Europe for local low-latency reads; turn on write forwarding so the few European writes are forwarded to the single primary writer in us-east-1.

Put Amazon RDS Proxy in front of the cluster to pool and reuse the many short-lived Lambda connections, and send read-only queries to the reader endpoint (or a read-only proxy endpoint) so the idle replicas carry the reads.
Use failover promotion tiers: tier 0 (highest priority) on the large replica in AZ 2, tier 1 on the large replica in AZ 3, and a low-priority tier such as 15 on the small reporting replica.

Use the cluster's reader endpoint for read-only connections; it load-balances new connections across all available Aurora Replicas, including ones added later. Writes stay on the cluster (writer) endpoint.

Heterogeneous migration: AWS SCT converts the Oracle schema and PL/SQL code to PostgreSQL, and AWS DMS moves the data with full load plus ongoing replication (CDC) over the private connection for a short cutover.

Unplanned Regional outage: run a global database failover (managed failover allowing data loss) to the us-west-2 secondary; the global writer endpoint follows the new primary, so the applications need no change. Switchover needs a healthy primary.
Unpredictable, spiky load on both reads and writes: Aurora Serverless v2 for writer and readers with a low minimum and high maximum ACU range, so capacity follows load and you pay for what you use.

Migrate to Aurora PostgreSQL: Aurora Replicas share the cluster volume, so replica lag is typically milliseconds (under about 100 ms), up to 15 replicas behind one reader endpoint, same PostgreSQL SQL.

Add an Aurora Replica in a different AZ; Aurora then promotes it automatically on writer or AZ failure, typically within about 30 seconds, and the cluster endpoint follows. Without a replica Aurora must recreate the instance, which takes minutes.
Aurora global database: storage-based replication to a secondary Region with lag typically under a second (RPO seconds) and failover to the secondary in minutes (RTO minutes).
Planned move with both Regions healthy and no data loss: global database switchover (formerly managed planned failover); the global writer endpoint follows the new primary.

Create an Aurora read replica of the RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance, wait until replica lag is zero, stop writes, and promote it to a standalone Aurora cluster; downtime is only the cutover minutes. Same engine, so no SCT needed.

Backtrack the Aurora MySQL cluster in place to just before the job; it rewinds the same cluster within the backtrack window in minutes, without restoring a new cluster, and the endpoints stay the same.
Key-value access by session ID, no joins, durable, spiky millions of requests: Amazon DynamoDB (on-demand) with session ID as partition key.

Create an Aurora custom endpoint whose static members are the two large replicas and send the analytics queries to it; the reader endpoint would spread them over all replicas, including the small ones.

Add an Aurora Replica in another AZ of us-east-1 for automatic in-Region failover, and make the cluster the primary of an Aurora global database with a secondary cluster in us-west-2 for cross-Region recovery with an RPO of seconds.
Steady, predictable load for 3 or more years: provisioned DB instances sized for that load, covered by 3-year Reserved Instances.
